name: Databricks SQL
tagline: Serverless SQL warehouses on the Databricks lakehouse, powered by the Photon C++ engine.
description: Databricks SQL is the warehousing layer of the Databricks platform: SQL warehouses (classic, pro or serverless) run the vectorized Photon engine directly over Delta Lake and Iceberg tables governed by Unity Catalog. Because the data stays in open formats in your cloud storage, the same tables serve Spark jobs, ML and BI without copies. It adds materialized views, streaming tables, AI functions and predictive optimization. It is strongest for organizations already on Databricks that want to retire a separate warehouse; for pure SQL shops it can feel like more platform than they need.

pricing.startingPrice: Serverless SQL from ~$0.70 per DBU (plus cloud costs for classic)
pricing.notes: Billed in DBUs per warehouse size and uptime; Databricks Free Edition available for learning.

scale.notes: Warehouses autoscale clusters for concurrency; storage is your own object storage, so capacity is effectively unbounded.

strengths: Warehouse over open Delta Lake/Iceberg tables in your own cloud storage
Photon vectorized engine gives strong price/performance on large scans
Unity Catalog provides one governance layer for SQL, ML and AI assets
Serverless warehouses start in seconds and scale for concurrency
Streaming tables and materialized views for incremental pipelines
weaknesses: DBU pricing plus underlying cloud costs is hard to forecast
Platform breadth means a steeper learning curve for SQL-only teams
Small, frequent writes create small-file and optimization overhead
useCases: Lakehouse SQL and BI on Delta Lake
Consolidating a separate warehouse into Databricks
Serving features and aggregates for ML
notIdealFor: Sub-second user-facing analytics at high QPS
Small teams with only a few GB of data
